[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

[STD-APP-ACC-001](../../../../standards/application/accessibility/STD-APP-ACC-001-accessibility.md) defines WCAG 2.2 AA requirements for all enterprise applications, but no React-specific implementation guidance exists. Development teams building accessible React components must rediscover the same patterns for ARIA, keyboard navigation, focus management, and automated testing — resulting in inconsistent implementations and recurring accessibility audit findings.
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

This guidance provides React-specific implementation steps for each WCAG 2.2 AA requirement category:

1. **Semantic HTML** — use native HTML elements before ARIA
2. **ARIA attributes** — correct role, state, and property usage in React components
3. **Keyboard navigation** — Tab/Shift-Tab, arrow keys, Escape, and Enter/Space handling
4. **Focus management** — focus trap for modals, focus restoration after dismissal, skip links
5. **axe-core integration** — automated accessibility testing in Vitest unit tests and Playwright E2E tests

This guidance leverages **Radix UI primitives** (via [ADR-APP-003](../../../../decisions/application/ADR-APP-003-ui-component-system-selection.md)) to provide WCAG 2.2 AA keyboard and ARIA behavior by default, with guidance on how to compose those primitives correctly.
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#when-to-use-this-guidance]

### When to Use This Guidance

- Building any new React component that will be presented to end users
- Reviewing an existing component for accessibility compliance
- Setting up axe-core automated accessibility testing in a new project
- Implementing custom components that extend beyond Radix UI / Shadcn/UI primitives
page_texts.7:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- **Compliance by default**: Radix UI primitives handle keyboard navigation and ARIA so developers do not re-implement them
- **Shift-left testing**: axe-core catches violations in CI before they reach QA or production
- **Audit-ready**: Components built with this pattern satisfy STD-APP-ACC-001 and Section 508 requirements
- **Reduced rework**: Patterns prevent the most common WCAG 2.2 violations found in healthcare UI audits

---
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Healthcare applications at Gainwell serve users across a wide range of abilities, including state agency staff, healthcare providers, and beneficiaries. Regulatory requirements (Section 508, ADA) mandate accessible applications. WCAG 2.2 AA is the current W3C standard and the compliance target defined in STD-APP-ACC-001.

Accessibility violations identified in production audits are significantly more expensive to remediate than violations caught during development. Each failing component in a micro-frontend can propagate violations across all host applications that consume it via Module Federation.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

The enterprise component stack (ADR-APP-003) uses **Radix UI** headless primitives, which implement WCAG-compliant keyboard navigation and ARIA roles out of the box. Shadcn/UI copies Radix-based components into each application's codebase. This pattern addresses:

- How to use those primitives correctly (not override their accessibility behavior)
- How to handle scenarios not covered by Radix primitives (custom components, dynamic content)
- How to integrate axe-core so violations are caught in CI
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Without implementation guidance:

- Developers override Radix UI's `asChild` prop or remove ARIA attributes that are required for screen readers
- Custom form components do not associate labels with inputs, producing WCAG 1.3.1 (Info and Relationships) violations
- Modal dialogs do not trap focus, producing WCAG 2.2.2 (No Keyboard Trap — reversed: focus must be trapped inside a modal) violations
- Focus is not restored when dialogs close, producing a disorienting experience for keyboard users
- Automated accessibility testing is not added to the test suite, so violations are not detected until manual audits

page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#pattern-overview]

### Pattern Overview

The accessible component pattern is organized into five capability areas, each mapped to the WCAG 2.2 success criteria it satisfies:

| Capability Area    | WCAG 2.2 Success Criteria                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Semantic HTML      | 1.3.1, 4.1.1, 4.1.2                                    |
| ARIA attributes    | 4.1.2, 1.3.1, 1.3.5                                    |
| Keyboard navigation| 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.4.3, 2.4.7                             |
| Focus management   | 2.4.3, 2.4.7, 3.2.2                                    |
| Automated testing  | All — validation gate for all above criteria           |

[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#1-semantic-html]

### 1. Semantic HTML

Use native HTML elements with their built-in semantics before reaching for ARIA roles.
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#2-aria-attributes]

### 2. ARIA Attributes

Apply ARIA attributes only when native HTML semantics are insufficient.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#3-keyboard-navigation]

### 3. Keyboard Navigation

All interactive functionality must be operable via keyboard alone (WCAG 2.2.1).
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#radix-ui-keyboard-behavior-built-in]

#### Radix UI Keyboard Behavior (Built-In)

Radix UI primitives implement correct keyboard behavior by default. Do **not** override these with custom `onKeyDown` handlers unless the behavior is intentionally extended:

| Radix Component        | Built-in keyboard behavior                                   |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Dialog`               | Escape closes; focus trapped inside; restored on close       |
| `DropdownMenu`         | Arrow keys navigate items; Escape closes; Enter/Space select |
| `Select`               | Arrow keys navigate options; Home/End; type-ahead            |
| `Tabs`                 | Arrow keys switch tabs; Home/End                             |
| `Accordion`            | Arrow keys navigate; Enter/Space expand/collapse             |
| `Checkbox`             | Space toggles; works with native form submission             |
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#4-focus-management]

### 4. Focus Management

Focus must be managed explicitly when the DOM structure changes in ways that move or remove the user's current focus position.

page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#ci-gate-configuration]

#### CI Gate Configuration

Add accessibility testing to the CI pipeline so violations block merges:

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml (excerpt)
- name: Run accessibility tests
  run: npx vitest run --reporter=verbose src/**/__tests__/*.test.tsx
  env:
    CI: true

- name: Run Playwright accessibility E2E
  run: npx playwright test e2e/accessibility/
```
page_texts.39:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#standards-alignment]

### Standards Alignment

This guidance implements the requirements of [STD-APP-ACC-001](../../../../standards/application/accessibility/STD-APP-ACC-001-accessibility.md) as prescribed by [PTN-APP-FE-001](../../../../patterns/application/frontend/PTN-APP-FE-001-accessible-component-pattern.md). Every React component delivered to end users must satisfy:

- **STD-APP-ACC-001 §2.1** — WCAG 2.2 AA compliance
- **STD-APP-ACC-001 §3.1** — Semantic HTML
- **STD-APP-ACC-001 §3.2** — ARIA Implementation
- **STD-APP-ACC-001 §3.3** — Keyboard Navigation
- **STD-APP-ACC-001 §3.4** — Focus Management
- **STD-APP-ACC-001 §5.1** — Automated Testing
page_texts.40:
[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#review-checklist]

### Review Checklist

Before submitting a component for code review, verify:

- [ ] Native HTML element used where one exists (no `<div role="button">`)
- [ ] All `<input>`, `<select>`, and `<textarea>` elements have an associated `<label>` (via `htmlFor`)
- [ ] Error messages use `role="alert"` or `aria-live="polite"` and are associated via `aria-describedby`
- [ ] All interactive elements are reachable by Tab and operable by Enter/Space
- [ ] Dialogs and modals use Radix UI `Dialog` (focus trap and Escape are built-in)
- [ ] Focus is returned to the trigger element when a dialog or menu closes
- [ ] Skip link is present on every page layout
- [ ] axe-core unit test passes with zero violations for the component
- [ ] Color contrast meets WCAG 1.4.3 (4.5:1 for normal text; 3:1 for large text)
- [ ] Icons used decoratively have `aria-hidden="true"`; icons with meaning have an accessible label

[strategy/guidance/application/accessibility/GUID-APP-ACC-001-accessible-component-implementation-guidance.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

1. Use native HTML elements; reach for ARIA only when no native element exists
2. Associate all form inputs with labels via `htmlFor`/`id`; associate error messages via `aria-describedby`
3. Use Radix UI / Shadcn/UI primitives — they handle keyboard navigation and focus trap for you
4. Add a skip link as the first focusable element on every page
5. Run `axe` in unit tests and Playwright E2E with `wcag22aa` tag; violations block CI
